title: Transportation:
format: 16:9 · 1920×1080 for V1 (client ask). 9:16 comes later as a separate version.
headline: A dad loved Sunday drives with his daughter. After his leukemia diagnosis, the car sits, and getting to treatment is not sure anymore.
story: Marcus and his little girl, in the back seat and on the road. That is where they talk. Then the car is parked and the tyre is flat, because every dollar now goes to staying alive. He waits at a bus stop with his medicine in a clear bag.

This is a Side Effects short. The client asked for this series to be serious and heavy: “leave you a little shaken by the gravity of them.” So the hopeful-only rule does not apply here. Warm at the start, cold at the end. No happy turn.
do: Open on picture with VO 1 on frame 1. No card, no logo, no black.
Use the straight-on look to camera (C056 / C054). The client asked for it by name.
Grade warm for the drive, then cold from the flat tyre on.
Use the client's VO words exactly. Male, traditional, serious narrator.
Keep the music low and simple. No lift, no build.
dont: No bright or friendly narrator. No upbeat music.
No logo or Family Reach text before the end cards.
No close-up of the medicine bottle labels. The names on them are wrong.
No crew voices (“action”, “look in the camera”).
No stock footage, no hospital shots, no lower-thirds.

bp_intro: Source clips are the Day 2 proxies A002_12050126_C043 to A002_12050237_C061 (1920×1080, 23.976 fps). There is no dialogue: the VO is the client's script, read by a narrator. Clip times are in seconds inside each proxy, from frames pulled from the real files and from visual.json. Every frame shown is from the real proxy, before the grade (it looks flat because it is RAW).

rows.frame_alt: Dad leans into the back seat toward his daughter
rows.visual: Back seat of the green car. Dad leans in to his daughter (glasses, white T-shirt). Start on frame 1 with both of them in shot. Warm grade.
rows.motion: Picture only. Nothing written on screen.

voice.quote: Marcus has always loved taking Sunday drives with his daughter.

rows.sfx: Car interior room tone from C048. No whoosh.
rows.music: Very low, warm, simple. One instrument.

rows.frame_alt: Dad in a pink shirt driving, looking up
rows.visual: Dad at the wheel, pink shirt, city outside. This shot is around 2:55–3:05 in C047, not at the start of the clip.

voice.quote: It's where they have their best conversations.

rows.sfx: Real car sound under the VO.

rows.frame_alt: Daughter in the back seat looking out
rows.visual: The girl in the back seat, looking out. Option: the shot of her reaching forward and smiling at about 2:40 (C047 ≈160 s).

voice.who: Dad and daughter (real car audio, low)
voice.quote: Yeah, remember? Look at the park. Remember where we go? … Yeah, where we go sledding.

rows.sfx: Their real voices, low, no captions. This is the last warm moment.

rows.frame_alt: Green sedan parked on a city street
rows.visual: The green sedan parked on the street. Still frame, no move. The warm grade ends on this cut.

rows.frame_alt: Front wheel of the green car, tyre still full
rows.visual: The front wheel (C043 3.8–11.5 s). The tyre is full in the footage. Make it go flat in post (David planned this as a post effect). Grade turns cold here.
rows.motion: Flat-tyre effect only. Keep it real and slow. No cartoon squash.

voice.quote: But after his leukemia diagnosis, every dollar went toward staying alive.

rows.sfx: Low air hiss as the tyre drops. Quiet.

rows.frame_alt: Dad in a beanie walks past the parked car with a bag
rows.visual: Dad, now in a beanie, walks past the parked car carrying his bag. Alternate: C049 5.2–15.5 s, same action, wider.

rows.frame_alt: Dad standing alone at a bus stop shelter
rows.visual: Wide: he stands alone at the bus stop. visual.json says a bus passes in C057 (7.5–22.4 s). Find the pass on scrub. If no clean pass, hold this wide.

voice.quote: Now getting to treatment isn't guaranteed.

rows.sfx: Bus pass, if it is in the shot.

rows.visual: The clear backpack with his medicine. Do not use this close shot as is: the bottle labels are readable and the crew said the names are wrong. Use the wider C061 (14.9–20.0 s) or blur the labels.

rows.frame_alt: Close-up: dad in a beanie looks straight into the lens
rows.visual: Close-up, he looks straight into the lens (C056 22.9–30.7 s). This is the “straight on look” the client asked for. Hold it. Alternate: medium at the bus stop sign, C054 27.1–36.2 s.
Black 1 s. Art card 1, 3 s. Art card 2, 3 s. Match the card style of the Utilities cut (“Emma's Drawing”).
rows.motion: Art card 1: <q>The side effects of cancer aren't always medical.</q> Art card 2: the Family Reach 30 Year logo, new brand only.
rows.music: One low note under the cards, then out.
